questions.stem: How do root hair cells absorb mineral ions from the soil when the concentration of minerals is higher inside the root than in the soil?

options.text: By osmosis through the partially permeable membrane
By diffusion down the concentration gradient
By active transport, using energy to move minerals against the concentration gradient
By evaporation pulling minerals up from the soil

questions.explanation: Mineral ions in the soil are often at a lower concentration than inside the root hair cell. Since diffusion cannot move substances against a concentration gradient, the cell uses active transport, powered by ATP from respiration, to absorb these essential minerals.
